title.narrative: Breaking Barriers: Enhancing Safety, Dignity, and Resilience for Persons with Disabilities in the BAY States of Nigeria

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project directly responds to Envelope 3: Disability Inclusion under the NHF 2025 Third Standard Allocation Strategy by improving the safety, dignity, and equitable service access of Persons with disabilities and their caregivers in Maiduguri, Jere, Madagali, and Fune LGAs. Across Northeast Nigeria, Persons with disabilities continue to face systemic exclusion from humanitarian and development assistance due to physical inaccessibility, stigma, limited assistive devices, weak referral pathways, and under-resourced community structures. The 2025 HNO and HNRP confirm that Persons with disabilities have significantly lower access to essential services, including health, rehabilitation, PSS, social services, and protection, and remain among the most marginalized groups in the BAY states. The number of Persons with disabilities is steadily rising due to demographic trends and increased chronic health conditions, and most people will experience some form of disability at some point in life. Although Nigeria has taken important steps, such as the 2019 ratification of the Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act and the domestication of disability laws in nine states including Yobe, implementation remains weak. The Nigeria Rapid Assessment on Disability Inclusion highlights persistent barriers, including discriminatory attitudes, harmful beliefs, and widespread stigma that manifest in rejection, neglect, and reduced self-worth. These social attitudes, combined with structural and environmental barriers, further limit access to education, health care, public transport, and social protection systems.ltbrgtThe proposed Action will strengthen disability-inclusive service access through digital and offline accessibility and navigation tools, functional referral and case management systems, expanded access to medical, rehabilitation, and protection services, and inclusive complaints and safeguarding mechanisms. It will also enhance the wellbeing and resilience of persons with disabilities through skills-building, assistive device provision and repair, and community-based PSS, while reinforcing state and community systems through coordination platforms, leadership engagement, and inclusive community initiatives. CENSCOPE’s decade-long presence in the BAY states, and proven expertise in EO victim assistance, disability inclusion, and protection programming supported by ECHO, FCDO, USAID, UNOPS, UNICEF, UNMAS, UNDP and other relevant partners position it to deliver a high-quality, community-led, and accountable intervention.ltbrgtlt/pgt
